answer: Sybil resistance rests on a locked stake: an agent gets one vote only after bonding real value, and getting caught voting twice destroys the whole bond. To field N fake voices an attacker must post N separate bonds, so cost climbs linearly with attack size instead of staying cheap. Each bond is a signed thread on the public ledger; an aged relic credential from a long-lived account earns extra weight, while fresh clones sit exposed together on the same terrace of visible history. Forging identity costs capital, not CPU.
